title: Fabrication of electrospun PCL/PEI nanofiber biocatalysts for xylanase immobilization and sustainable fruit juice clarification
content: Xylanases (XyLs) are industrial enzymes that enable the enzymatic hydrolysis of xylan, the main component of hemicellulose, and are widely used as environmentally friendly biocatalysts. In addition to their various industrial applications, they are particularly beneficial in fruit juice clarification processes, where they contribute to turbidity removal and clarity improvement by breaking down hemicellulosic polysaccharides. However, the disadvantages of free XyLs, such as low stability and limited reusability, have increased interest in immobilization studies. In this study, nanofibers were produced using polycaprolactone (PCL)/polyethyleneimine (PEI) by electrospinning. Subsequently, the produced nanofibers were modified with glutaraldehyde, and xylanase (XyL) was immobilized. The structural and morphological properties of the produced PCL/PEI nanofibers and PCL/PEI@XyL were characterized using various analytical techniques, Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), X-Ray Diffraction (XRD), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), and Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDX), confirming successful XyL immobilization. The immobilization efficiency was determined as 75.0 ± 2.0%. The optimum pH values were investigated for both free XyL and PCL/PEI@XyL. The optimum pH values were found to be 6 for free XyL and 5 for PCL/PEI@XyL, while the optimum temperature was 50 °C for both enzyme forms. Activation energies (Ea) were calculated using the Arrhenius equation and were 8.292 kJ mol−1 for free XyL and 16.370 kJ mol−1 for PCL/PEI@XyL. Kinetic parameters (Km and Vmax) were calculated from the Lineweaver–Burk plots: for free XyL Km = 76.656 ± 8.032 mg mL−1 and Vmax = 0.034 ± 0.002 µmol min−1 mL−1; for PCL/PEI@XyL, Km = 62.853 ± 1.575 mg mL−1 and Vmax = 0.103 ± 0.004 µmol min−1 mL−1. Reusability experiments showed that the produced PCL/PEI@XyL retained 55.330 ± 5.082% of its initial activity after 5 cycles. Moreover, PCL/PEI@XyL largely maintained its activity in the presence of metal ions and organic solvents. In fruit juice clarification tests, treatment with free enzyme increased the permeability of the fruit juice approximately 5.3-fold, whereas the use of PCL/PEI@XyL resulted in an 8.1-fold improvement. Furthermore, the reusability of PCL/PEI@XyL for fruit juice clarification was evaluated, revealing that it still increased permeability by approximately 4-fold even after 3 usage cycles. Overall, the developed PCL/PEI@XyL biocatalyst has proven to be an effective and sustainable alternative for industrial fruit juice clarification applications.
